title: Remove the unreachable single-team mode from the timeslot booking form
request: Owner pasted the DeepSource Test coverage report for PR 1730: it fails on src/components/timeslots/TimeslotAssignment.tsx lines 130, 171-173 and 210, which no test can reach because batchMode is always true. Fix it (owner standing rule: fix everything that comes up).

criteria.text: The unreachable code is removed from the timeslot booking form (the single-team drop-down branch, its submit branch, the single-time branch of the double header toggle, and the state only they used) and nothing else on the form changes: markup, Confirm text and Confirm enabled state are the same in 7 form states at 390px and at 1280px wide before and after, and the form's tests pass.
criteria.evidence: Before and after snapshots of the real form (fake data, headless Chromium, dev server): 7 states at 390px and 7 at 1280px wide (empty, team ticked, block picked, double header on, one time, two times, Select All). All 14 are byte-identical in markup, Confirm text and Confirm disabled flag. The 72 tests in src/components/timeslots and src/components/admin/timeslots pass; typecheck and lint pass on the changed file. Diff: 37 added, 93 removed, one source file.

criteria.text: Line coverage of TimeslotAssignment.tsx is 100% in the unit tests, and the DeepSource Test coverage status on the pushed head no longer lists that file.
criteria.evidence: Local: line coverage of TimeslotAssignment.tsx is 100% (52 of 52 lines) from its own tests. On GitHub: DeepSource Test coverage on the PR head 506515d (same source as the code commit d463411; only .factory files differ) reports success at 13:01 UTC with the text 'Analysis passed: No blocking issues or failing metrics found' (run f3b4fe39). Before this change it failed on lines 130, 171-173 and 210. The PR's combined commit status is now success for the first time: React Doctor success (one known warning), DeepSource JavaScript success, DeepSource Test coverage success.

criteria.text: Six checks pass at the final head and an independent code review approves. The unused onAssign prop chain through TimeslotsTab and the hook is left as it is, and named as a follow-up.
criteria.evidence: Six checks pass at d463411 (integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit; none dirty). Independent code review: APPROVE at d463411 (60 random click sequences identical old vs new, 768-combination truth table matched, snapshots byte-identical). The onAssign chain is left as it is and recorded as a follow-up note on this task.

reviews.summary: Independent reviewer (fresh, read-only) tried to break five claims and could not. (1) batchMode was useState(true) with the setter never called, so the single-team drop-down, its submit branch and its label never ran. (2) handleTimeslotToggle is wired only to the double header buttons, so its single-time branch never ran. (3) A truth table of 768 combinations of the Confirm disabled rule and label matched old and new, and a differential run of 60 seeded random click sequences (team ticks, Select All, block pick, Double Header switch, time buttons, submit, re-renders with 4 booking sets) gave identical innerHTML and identical onBatchAssign and onBatchAssignDoubleHeaders calls at every step (38 batch and 9 double header bookings); a deliberate break of the rule made 14 of 60 fail, so the check can fail. (4) onAssign stays in the type so TimeslotsTab compiles; nothing else depends on the removed drop-down. (5) Before and after form snapshots are byte-identical across 14 distinct states. Tests (54) pass, eslint clean, line coverage of the file 100% (52/52). Follow-up named: remove the unused onAssign chain (TimeslotsTab handleTimeslotAssign, the onAssign prop, the hook addTimeslot) in a separate task.

notes.text: Follow-up, not done here: onAssign is now unused inside TimeslotAssignment. Remove the chain in a separate small task: TimeslotsTab handleTimeslotAssign (line ~221, passed at ~413), the onAssign prop type, the hook useTimeslotMutation addTimeslot (and its service and tests if nothing else uses them). Two older audit docs cite the old line numbers (bug-triage.md:1456, docs/audits/UX-AUDIT-2026-09.md:392); they are dated records and were not changed.
